text:
maria: FYI alert — we've got a ~18% token/sec regression on prod after last rollout (suspect windowed scheduler tweak). Telemetry shows throughput 120k tok/s -> 98k tok/s on continuous-batcher fleet. Putting rollout on hold. @kenji @sam can you triage? :eyes:

infra-bot: perf CI job 'throughput/continuous-batcher' failed on main — median tokens/sec drop > threshold. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234 :robot_face:

kenji: I started a quick bisect on the staging image. Narrowed it to the scheduler heuristic change in commit b7f4c9a (PR #4257) that adjusted the batch fill window and changed kernel hinting logic.

sam: quick numbers from a fresh probe on a representative host (p100x-enc1):
- before (main@a1b2c3d): token/sec 121k, avg latency p50 72ms
- after (main@b7f4c9a): token/sec 99k, avg latency p50 90ms
KV cache hitrate fell 0.82 -> 0.68 for the same traffic slice. Looks correlated.

elaine: profile dump shows extra time spent in kernel selection path and memcpy churn. Flame summary (diff b7f4c9a vs a1b2c3d):
```
+ 12% scheduler:select_kernel
+ 8% runtime:kv_cache->lookup (misses up)
+ 6% memcopy (small-batch path)
- 4% batching:coalescer (less effective)
```
Not proof, but suggests the heuristic is causing more small batches and cache churn.

kenji: actionable bisect steps I ran:
```
git checkout a1b2c3d && run perf harness (good)
git checkout b7f4c9a && run perf harness (bad)
# bisect narrowed to scheduler/heuristic file scheduler/window_policy.cc
```
I also toggled the kernel-hint flag to force old kernel selection; that recovers ~6% of throughput but not all.

sam: interesting — I noticed the scheduler started emitting slightly different batch size distribution: more 1-2 token batches during peak. Plot attached (saved to S3) — shift in mass to tiny batches explains memcopy overhead. Could be the greedy-fill change and an unintended interaction with prefix/KV caching.

maria: can someone open an immediate revert PR for the heuristic change? We should hold host-level deploys until we confirm. This is causing customer-visible latency. :warning:

kenji: opened a revert PR #4333 and added perf backfill steps + CI job rerun. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/4333 — request review from @elaine and @sam. I set rollout to blocked in console.

perf-bot: rerun: throughput/continuous-batcher (staging) triggered by PR #4333. Job queued.

elaine: small experiment: forcing larger coalescing window in runtime config recovers both KV hitrate (0.78) and token/sec (~116k) on staging. Config snippet I used:
```
{"scheduler": {"coalesce_window_ms": 12, "greedy_fill": false},
 "kv_cache": {"shard_hash_v2": false}}
```
We should consider a two-step fix: revert to previous heuristic, then rework kernel-hint change in a follow-up that includes KV cache invariants and more unit tests.

sam: agree. Also adding a perf test that emits the tiny-batch pattern would have caught this. I'll add a focused e2e perf run to the PR checklist.

maria: plan: 1) hold rollout (done), 2) revert PR #4333 merge ASAP, 3) run backfill perf on canaries for 4h, 4) after green, resume gradual rollout. I'll update status in the release thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: rollout state: HOLD (reason: perf regression). Blocking tickets: #INT-7892.

kenji: after merge/revert I'll run a bisect on the kernel-hint lines and submit a targeted follow-up that adds KV-cache regression tests.

maria: leaving this open until we've got green backfill and monitoring for 24h post-revert. Ping me on pager if token/sec drops again.
